scope: Execution study on one GH200 node (four GPUs, one solve per GPU at a time): complete solves of the 2D Kovasznay objective with the unchanged solve.py optimizer program, where torch.optim.LBFGS either runs as installed (cell stock) or with only its two-loop recursion replaced by a device-side, CUDA-Graph-replayed version (cell light). Native GL8 (gl8_native) in FP64 at 2,048, 16,384 and 65,536 interior points on the six formal initializations. GH200 numbers only; nothing is pooled with the H100 or H20 campaigns.
motivation: Post hoc, the H100 solve-scale archives put 93% of the 2,048-point optimization time into the L-BFGS phase outside the gradient; torch.optim.LBFGS converts each two-loop coefficient to a host number (about 109 device synchronizations per iteration). A development run on GH200 (three stock/light pairs) gave bitwise-identical final parameters and 2.83x, 2.40x (2,048 points) and 1.49x (65,536 points) shorter optimization.

source.unchanged: bench_gpu.py, gpu_engine.py, problem.py, solve.py and every flashns module

runtime.note: LightLBFGS rewrites the installed LBFGS.step source and refuses a module whose two-loop block differs

light.difference: two-loop recursion only: coefficients stay on the device (Triton kernel, one fma per element, matching add_(alpha=) bitwise), ring buffer of the full history, one captured CUDA Graph per ring position

optimizer_program: unchanged solve.py: 4,000 Adam updates, strong-Wolfe L-BFGS in blocks of at most 20 iterations / 25 evaluations, history 50, stop checks before training, every 100 Adam updates and after every block, 500-block extension as in bench_gpu.complete_solve
acceptance: unchanged: all six metrics on the fixed 8,192-point validation set and the independent scalar-AD set; a non-converged solve is a failed solve
prebuild: before the queue, on lane 0: one light solve at 2,048 points (seed 862101), not scored, so the native extension and the Triton kernels are compiled once and every timed task starts warm

tasks.solves: 2 cells x 3 sizes x 6 seeds = 36, one fresh process each, pre-randomized order over four lanes
tasks.drift: the first four tasks of the randomized order are repeated at the end as drift-<id>

per_size: count of pairs with identical final parameter SHA-256, evaluation count, L-BFGS iteration count and acceptance
paired geometric mean (and range) of stock over light optimization-only seconds over jointly accepted pairs
paired geometric mean of setup plus optimization seconds
pairs favouring light in optimization time
L-BFGS-phase and Adam-phase milliseconds per evaluation per cell (medians)
drift: each repeat identical to its first run (same fields as above)
optimization time of each repeat within 5% of its first run

per_size.EXECUTION_GAIN_IDENTICAL: all six pairs identical and jointly accepted, geometric mean stock/light optimization > 1.03, at least 5 of 6 pairs favour light
per_size.IDENTICAL_NO_GAIN: all six pairs identical and jointly accepted, otherwise
per_size.TRAJECTORY_DIFFERS: any pair not identical: no execution claim at that size; the differing seeds are listed

decision_rule.validity: a drift repeat that is not identical, or outside 5%, marks the whole batch NOT_VALID for timing (identity results stand)

predictions.note: expectations, not gates, from the development pairs and the H100 phase model

frozen_inputs.platform_note: problem.parameters(seed) draws torch.randn on the CPU; torch's CPU normal sampler is not bitwise identical between x86-64 (the H20/H100 studies) and aarch64 (the GH200 node's Grace CPU), so the GH200 formal initializations of the six seeds are the aarch64 draws, pinned here from a dedicated check job on a GH200 node (torch 2.14.1+cu130). The collocation data (torch.rand) are bitwise identical on both platforms, as the data hashes show. Attempt 1 (v1 protocol, x86 hashes) was refused at admission before any GPU work.

execution.node: one GH200 node, four GPUs, one task per GPU at a time
